<cell id="4deaeb53"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Visualize the relationship

Plot listed price against positive review ratio and add a fitted trend line to show the overall relationship. Point size represents each game's total rating volume.</cell id="4deaeb53">
<cell id="6064034f">import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    n=min(20_000, len(steam)),
    random_state=42,
)

x = plot_data["price"]
y = plot_data["positive_ratio"]

slope, intercept = np.polyfit(
    x,
    y,
    1,
)

x_line = np.linspace(
    x.min(),
    x.max(),
    200,
)

point_sizes = (
    np.log1p(
        plot_data["total_ratings"]
    )
    * 3
)


fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 6)
)

ax.scatter(
    x,
    y,
    s=point_sizes,
    alpha=0.15,
)

ax.plot(
    x_line,
    slope * x_line + intercept,
    linewidth=2,
)

ax.set_title(
    "Game Price and Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Game Price"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

ax.text(
    0.03,
    0.96,
    (
        f"Pearson r = {corr:.3f}\n"
        f"p = {p_value:.3g}"
    ),
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    va="top",
)

ax.text(
    0.97,
    0.04,
    "Point size reflects\ntotal rating volume",
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    ha="right",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9,
)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plot_data = steam.sample(
    n=min(20_000, len(steam)),
    random_state=42,
)

x = plot_data["price"]
y = plot_data["positive_ratio"]

slope, intercept = np.polyfit(
    x,
    y,
    1,
)

x_line = np.linspace(
    x.min(),
    x.max(),
    200,
)

point_sizes = (
    np.log1p(
        plot_data["total_ratings"]
    )
    * 3
)

point_colors = np.log1p(
    plot_data["average_playtime"]
)


fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 6)
)

scatter = ax.scatter(
    x,
    y,
    s=point_sizes,
    c=point_colors,
    cmap="viridis",
    alpha=0.35,
)

ax.plot(
    x_line,
    slope * x_line + intercept,
    linewidth=2,
    color="black",
)

ax.set_title(
    "Game Price and Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Game Price"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

cbar = fig.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label("Average Playtime (log1p scale)")

ax.text(
    0.03,
    0.96,
    (
        f"Pearson r = {corr:.3f}\n"
        f"p = {p_value:.3g}"
    ),
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    va="top",
)

ax.text(
    0.97,
    0.04,
    "Point size reflects\ntotal rating volume",
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    ha="right",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9,
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

## Calculate the playtime-rating correlation

Calculate the Pearson correlation between average playtime and positive review ratio. Games with an average playtime of 0 are excluded, since SteamSpy reports 0 when it lacks enough data to estimate playtime rather than a genuine zero. Playtime is log-transformed before computing the correlation because it is heavily right-skewed.

content.text: Now let's update the Conclusion to incorporate this new finding.

input.new_source:
## Conclusion

The analysis finds a weak positive correlation between listed game price and positive review ratio (**r ≈ 0.076**).

This suggests that higher-priced games tend to receive slightly better user ratings on average, although the relationship is weak.

Average playtime (log-transformed, among games with tracked playtime) shows a similarly weak positive correlation with positive review ratio (**r ≈ 0.123**), and is somewhat more strongly associated with positive reception than price is. This is consistent with the idea that players who stick around longer tend to rate a game more favorably, though playtime still explains only a small share of the variation in ratings.

playtime_plot_data = steam_with_playtime.sample(
    n=min(20_000, len(steam_with_playtime)),
    random_state=42,
)

x_playtime = playtime_plot_data["log_playtime"]
y_playtime = playtime_plot_data["positive_ratio"]

playtime_slope, playtime_intercept = np.polyfit(
    x_playtime,
    y_playtime,
    1,
)

x_playtime_line = np.linspace(
    x_playtime.min(),
    x_playtime.max(),
    200,
)

playtime_point_sizes = (
    np.log1p(
        playtime_plot_data["total_ratings"]
    )
    * 3
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 6)
)

ax.scatter(
    x_playtime,
    y_playtime,
    s=playtime_point_sizes,
    alpha=0.15,
)

ax.plot(
    x_playtime_line,
    playtime_slope * x_playtime_line + playtime_intercept,
    linewidth=2,
    color="black",
)

ax.set_title(
    "Average Playtime and Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Average Playtime (log1p scale)"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

ax.text(
    0.03,
    0.96,
    (
        f"Pearson r = {playtime_corr:.3f}\n"
        f"p = {playtime_p_value:.3g}"
    ),
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    va="top",
)

ax.text(
    0.97,
    0.04,
    "Point size reflects\ntotal rating volume",
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    ha="right",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9,
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

content.text:
That clustering is real, not just an artifact of the scatter — I checked with decile bins: mean positive ratio bounces between ~0.68–0.80 through most of the middle of the playtime range and only rises clearly in the top decile. So the relationship genuinely is weak/flat except at the tails.

A binned view would show this more clearly than the dense scatter: bucket games into playtime deciles (or fixed log-spaced bins) and plot mean positive ratio per bucket (bar or line, with point size/error bars reflecting sample count). That removes the overplotting distortion and makes the "flat middle, uptick at high playtime" pattern visible instead of hidden in a cloud of overlapping points.

steam_with_playtime["playtime_decile"] = pd.qcut(
    steam_with_playtime["average_playtime"],
    10,
    duplicates="drop",
)

playtime_buckets = steam_with_playtime.groupby(
    "playtime_decile"
).agg(
    mean_positive_ratio=("positive_ratio", "mean"),
    median_playtime=("average_playtime", "median"),
    game_count=("positive_ratio", "size"),
).reset_index()

bucket_x = np.log1p(
    playtime_buckets["median_playtime"]
)

bucket_sizes = (
    playtime_buckets["game_count"]
    / playtime_buckets["game_count"].max()
) * 400

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 6)
)

ax.plot(
    bucket_x,
    playtime_buckets["mean_positive_ratio"],
    linewidth=2,
    color="black",
    zorder=1,
)

ax.scatter(
    bucket_x,
    playtime_buckets["mean_positive_ratio"],
    s=bucket_sizes,
    zorder=2,
)

ax.set_title(
    "Average Playtime and Positive Review Ratio (by decile)"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Median Playtime in Decile (log1p scale)"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Mean Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

ax.text(
    0.97,
    0.04,
    "Point size reflects\ngames per decile",
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    ha="right",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9,
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

playtime_buckets

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
df = pd.read_csv('../../data/steam/steam.csv')
df = df.dropna(subset=['price','positive_ratings','negative_ratings'])
df['total_ratings'] = df['positive_ratings']+df['negative_ratings']
df = df[df['total_ratings']>0]
df['positive_ratio'] = df['positive_ratings']/df['total_ratings']
print(df['price'].describe())
print(df['price'].quantile([0,.1,.25,.5,.75,.9,.95,.99,1]))
sub = df.copy()
sub['bin'] = pd.qcut(sub['price'], 10, duplicates='drop')
print(sub.groupby('bin')['positive_ratio'].agg(['mean','count']))
"

steam["price_decile"] = pd.qcut(
    steam["price"],
    10,
    duplicates="drop",
)

price_buckets = steam.groupby(
    "price_decile"
).agg(
    mean_positive_ratio=("positive_ratio", "mean"),
    median_price=("price", "median"),
    game_count=("positive_ratio", "size"),
).reset_index()

price_bucket_x = price_buckets["median_price"]

price_bucket_sizes = (
    price_buckets["game_count"]
    / price_buckets["game_count"].max()
) * 400

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 6)
)

ax.plot(
    price_bucket_x,
    price_buckets["mean_positive_ratio"],
    linewidth=2,
    color="black",
    zorder=1,
)

ax.scatter(
    price_bucket_x,
    price_buckets["mean_positive_ratio"],
    s=price_bucket_sizes,
    zorder=2,
)

ax.set_title(
    "Game Price and Positive Review Ratio (by decile)"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Median Price in Decile"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Mean Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

ax.text(
    0.97,
    0.04,
    "Point size reflects\ngames per decile",
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    ha="right",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9,
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

price_buckets

## Conclusion

The analysis finds a weak positive correlation between listed game price and positive review ratio (**r ≈ 0.076**).

This suggests that higher-priced games tend to receive slightly better user ratings on average, although the relationship is weak. Bucketing games into price deciles shows this trend more clearly than the raw scatter: mean positive review ratio rises fairly steadily from **≈0.68** in the cheapest decile to **≈0.76** in the upper-mid deciles, before leveling off among the most expensive games.

Average playtime (log-transformed, among games with tracked playtime) shows a similarly weak positive correlation with positive review ratio (**r ≈ 0.123**), and is somewhat more strongly associated with positive reception than price is. However, the decile view reveals this relationship is much less monotonic than price's: mean positive ratio bounces between **≈0.68–0.80** through most of the playtime range and only rises clearly in the top decile, meaning the correlation is driven mainly by the highest-playtime games rather than a steady trend across the whole range.

cd "/workspaces/human-AI-logs/tasks/task 3" && python3 -c "
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy.stats import pearsonr
df = pd.read_csv('../../data/steam/steam.csv')
df = df.dropna(subset=['price','positive_ratings','negative_ratings'])
df['total_ratings'] = df['positive_ratings']+df['negative_ratings']
df = df[df['total_ratings']>0]
df['positive_ratio'] = df['positive_ratings']/df['total_ratings']

# price deciles
price_bin = pd.qcut(df['price'], 10, duplicates='drop')
pb = df.groupby(price_bin).agg(mean_pr=('positive_ratio','mean'), med_price=('price','median')).reset_index()
r,p = pearsonr(pb['med_price'], pb['mean_pr'])
print('price decile-level corr', r, p, 'n=', len(pb))

sub = df[df['average_playtime']>0].copy()
pt_bin = pd.qcut(sub['average_playtime'], 10, duplicates='drop')
tb = sub.groupby(pt_bin).agg(mean_pr=('positive_ratio','mean'), med_pt=('average_playtime','median')).reset_index()
tb['log_med_pt'] = np.log1p(tb['med_pt'])
r2,p2 = pearsonr(tb['log_med_pt'], tb['mean_pr'])
print('playtime decile-level corr', r2, p2, 'n=', len(tb))
"
